tip.title: Never Click Unverified Links
tip.content: Do not click links in SMS messages from unknown senders. Legitimate organizations like banks and government agencies will never ask you to click a link to verify your account via text message.

tip.title: Urgency Is a Manipulation Tactic
tip.content: Scammers often use urgent language like "Act now," "Your account will be locked," or "Limited time only" to pressure you into clicking without thinking. Take a moment to verify before acting.

tip.title: Prize and Reward Messages Are Almost Always Scams
tip.content: Messages claiming you have won a prize, reward, or cash that you did not enter a contest for are almost certainly scams. Legitimate companies do not notify winners through unsolicited SMS messages.

tip.title: SIM Registration Did Not Stop Scammers
tip.content: Even with the SIM Registration Act in effect, scammers continue to send fraudulent messages using registered SIMs under false identities. Always evaluate the content of the message, not just the sender.

tip.title: Sender Names Can Be Faked
tip.content: Scammers can make SMS messages appear to come from trusted names like GCash, BDO, or government agencies. This is called Sender ID spoofing. Always read the message content carefully before taking any action.

tip.title: Report Suspicious Messages
tip.content: If you receive a suspicious SMS, report it using this app or forward it to the NTC or PNP Anti-Cybercrime Group. Reporting helps protect others in your community.

tip.title: Protect Your Personal Information
tip.content: Never share your full name, address, birthday, bank account number, credit card details, or government ID numbers in response to an SMS message. No legitimate institution will request this through text.

tip.title: Shortened URLs Are a Red Flag
tip.content: Be cautious of shortened links such as bit.ly or tinyurl.com in SMS messages. Scammers use these to hide the real destination of a link. When in doubt, do not click.

tip.title: Check the Domain Before Opening
tip.content: Look carefully at the website address before opening a link. Scam sites often use misspellings, extra characters, or domains that imitate legitimate companies.

tip.title: Avoid Links From Unknown Senders
tip.content: Do not open links sent by numbers or accounts you do not recognize. If the message claims to come from a company, visit its official website or app instead.

tip.title: HTTPS Does Not Always Mean Safe
tip.content: A padlock or HTTPS connection only means the connection is encrypted. Scam websites can also use HTTPS, so always check the domain and sender before entering any information.

tip.title: GCash and Banks Will Never Ask for Your OTP
tip.content: GCash, BDO, BPI, and other financial institutions will never ask for your One-Time Password (OTP), PIN, or password through SMS. If a message asks for these, it is a scam.

tip.title: Verify Suspicious Bank Alerts
tip.content: If you receive a message saying your account is locked or compromised, do not use the link in the message. Open the official banking app or contact the bank through its verified number.

tip.title: Watch for Fake Refund Messages
tip.content: Scammers may claim that you are entitled to a refund and ask for your card details or login information. Confirm refunds directly through the official bank or merchant application.

tip.title: Never Share Your PIN or Password
tip.content: Bank employees will never ask you to send your PIN, password, card security code, or online banking credentials through SMS. Keep these details private at all times.

tip.title: Verify Delivery Messages Through Official Apps
tip.content: If you receive an SMS about a parcel or delivery, do not click the link in the message. Instead, open the official website or app of the courier service and track your package directly there.

tip.title: Be Careful With Failed Delivery Messages
tip.content: Scammers may claim that a package could not be delivered and ask you to click a link to reschedule it. Check the courier's official app or website instead.

tip.title: Do Not Pay Unexpected Delivery Fees
tip.content: Be suspicious of messages asking for a small payment before a parcel can be delivered. Verify the tracking number directly with the courier before paying anything.

tip.title: Check the Tracking Number
tip.content: Fake delivery messages often contain invented or incomplete tracking information. Enter the tracking number manually on the courier's official website instead of opening a link from the SMS.
